lead: you have belonged to the same circle since your twenties, and the person you most want to see this week is somebody you met in the spring, whose whole shape you already have.
sun: the sorting does its work fast on a new person. inside a month of meeting someone you have them sorted — which part of them is carrying the rest, which enthusiasm is decoration, which of their friendships is real and which is a habit with a name on it. you are inside the acquaintance and slightly off it the whole time, and the sorting finishes long before the friendship has started.
moon: the appetite that took you toward them was for the finding. it runs forward, close to the ground, without dignity — you will cross a city to sit with somebody new — and it has nothing after it. the week you know them is the week it goes quiet. what is left is a person you like, correctly, at a temperature they can feel dropping.
pull: you have known your oldest friends for twenty years and you know all of them from the first six weeks. nothing since has been news.
tension: the charge that lands is that you collect people, and from where they stand the sequence looks exactly like collecting: the crossing town, the long evenings, then the sudden ordinary politeness. intense gets said about you in one half of a year and unreliable in the other, by the same person, describing one week. you cannot dispute the sequence. what you could say about it, that the finding was over, makes it worse in the room.
cost: you are the friend people bring a new person to when they want a read, and you give it in one evening and it holds. you never revise it; revising would take the years you did not spend. the people who have been in your life longest are held there by the circle rather than by you, and attendance is what those friendships run on.

lead: there is no hour when both of your lights are above the horizon. the moon comes up as the sun goes down, half the road apart, and nothing that happens at that end of you happens quietly.
sun: twelve years in that room and you have spent all twelve a step outside it, which is what lets you see which two of them are doing the work and which of the old stories is holding the rest up. nothing about that seeing is provisional. it lands whole, once, and is finished before you have decided whether to keep it.
moon: in the third year, across one meeting, a room you attend every week came apart inside you and stayed apart. you have said nothing since. the group is whole, you still turn up, and the order you settled that evening has not moved. it cannot be held lightly, softened, or gone back over, and nobody has been shown it.
pull: the group has never met the half of you that decided about it. it decided in one evening, years ago, and nothing since has been able to take any of it back.
tension: loyal is what gets said, and the attendance record supports it. you sit through the annual dinner with a settled account of who in that room is carrying it and who is carried, unable to soften the account by a grade and unable to say it without ending the evening permanently. so you are warm, and you are accurate, and the two never meet. people who have known you fifteen years call you easy.
cost: the account you keep of that room is exact in its particulars and has been since the third year, and no further evidence adjusts it. not even somebody changing. the person you placed lowest a decade ago has never been told, has nothing available to answer, and goes on being measured against a finding that was made once and closed.

lead: you came back to the trade at forty-one, eleven years after walking out, and within a month you could see which of its habits had died in your absence and who had been keeping the rest alive.
sun: the returning member sees the seams. the people who stayed watched every change arrive one at a time, which is what makes a practice invisible to them. you left, and came back holding the two versions side by side, so you know without being told which of the standing arrangements is load-bearing and which is one person's preference that outlived its reason. you are on the roll again, at the same angle you always were.
moon: coming back is the native motion, and while it was happening the leaving felt like an interval. it was eleven years. they went through a departure; you went through a gap, and you returned expecting the place to be where you left it, which in the parts that matter it was. you are the last one there who can still see the difference.
pull: they call it a return and mean you never really went. you went. what came back with you is the only measurement anybody there has of what the place used to be.
tension: the ones who stayed have a claim on it you cannot match and would not dispute, and they know precisely how long you were gone. so when you name the dead practice — the meeting nobody needs — it arrives as a criticism from somebody who was not there for the hard part. the observation is right. the standing to make it is what you spent eleven years not accruing, and both facts are obvious to everyone present.
cost: you can rejoin a thing you left and be genuinely inside it by the second winter, because leaving never registered with you as an ending and nothing in your manner asks to be forgiven for it. the same instinct is why the people you left behind got no goodbye worth the name. they had a departure; you had an interval; nobody has ever reconciled the two.

lead: nine years after the funeral the household still runs on him, and the version of him it runs on is one you could take apart in a sitting and have never touched.
sun: you were of that family and never entirely in it, and that is the position grief is least kind to. from where you stood you could watch the death sort them inside a week — who was bereaved and who was performing a part assigned decades earlier, which of the stories about him would be doing work by the second year and which would quietly go. you had it by the end of the wake.
moon: what the family lives on has no edges. from any distance it reads as one man they loved; closer in it comes apart into a dozen different men, one per person, each of them feeding somebody. the arrangement works. it is nourishing three households and a marriage, and it is not accurate, and the inaccuracy carries as much of the weight as anything true about him does.
pull: the dead man is the food. you can see what is in it and what is not, and pulling one thread would take the meal off the table for everybody sitting there.
tension: you are the one they describe as having taken it well, and the description rests entirely on your not having said anything. what you hold back is a single sentence: that in the year that mattered he was not the person the family needs him to have been. it is true and you can date it, and said out loud it would come apart along the line you named, taking his widow's account of her own marriage with it.
cost: in a room of grieving people you know which of them lost a person and which lost a position, you are right, and the knowledge has nowhere to go. so it sits with you through the anniversaries and keeps working. of everyone in that family you are the one who cannot stand at the grave without doing the arithmetic, and the arithmetic has never come out kind.
